pr.title: Bind MySQL command parameters as prepared statements (1.1c)
pr.body:
## Summary

Phase 1.1c: MySQL command parameters are now **bound as prepared statements** instead of being written into the SQL. This finishes the SQL-injection work of 1.1:

| Database | Before #9 | Now |
|---|---|---|
| SQL Server Compact | Bound | Bound |
| PostgreSQL | Inlined (injectable until #9) | Bound (#12) |
| MySQL via MariaDB Connector/C (what the installer ships) | Inlined (injectable until #9) | **Bound (this PR)** |
| MySQL via Oracle `libmysql.dll` (fallback when `libmariadb.dll` is missing) | Inlined (injectable until #9) | Inlined, escaped single-pass (#9); removed in 1.4 |

## How it works

- **`MySQLStatement` (new):** prepares, binds and executes a command with `mysql_stmt_*`, then reads the result set.
  - Every column is fetched as a string, so the recordset reads the rows exactly as it reads a query's rows.
  - Buffers are sized from `STMT_ATTR_UPDATE_MAX_LENGTH`; a longer value is fetched again in full with `mysql_stmt_fetch_column`.
  - It is the only file that includes the MariaDB headers (for `MYSQL_BIND` and `MYSQL_FIELD`), through per-file include directories. The functions are still resolved at run time through `MySQLInterface`.
- **`SQLStatement::ToPositionalParameters`** can also write MySQL's `?` placeholders: one per occurrence, so a parameter used twice is bound twice. A parameter inside a literal is still refused. `SQLStatementTester` covers both cases.
- **`MySQLConnection`:**
  - `GetSupportsCommandParameters()` is true when the MariaDB client is loaded and exports every statement function.
  - `TryExecute`, and `MySQLRecordset::TryOpen`, run a command that still has its parameters as a prepared statement.
  - Error numbers map the same way as on the query path: a lost connection is retried, and a duplicate key can be ignored by the caller.
- **Unchanged:** commands without parameters (`SET NAMES`, `USE`, `SHOW`, the internal scripts) are still sent as queries.

## Tests

`API.SqlValues`, a new regression test fixture that runs on every database:
- `TestTextValuesAreStoredAsGiven` stores and reads back text that contains quotes, backslashes, comment and statement markers, `@VALUE`, `@@ID`, `?`, `$1`, LIKE wildcards and non-ASCII characters.
- `TestLogonLooksUpTheAddressAsGiven` logs on as `o'brien@example.test`. A user name of `x' OR '1'='1` must not log on.

These are regression guards rather than reproductions: since #9, MySQL's inlined values were already escaped correctly.

## Notes

- A command with parameters now takes a prepare and an execute (two round trips) instead of one query. Caching prepared statements per connection is possible later if it ever shows up in profiles.
- The `upgrade-mariadb` skill now lists the include directories in `hMailServer.vcxproj` as version-pinned, and checks the `mysql_stmt_*` exports.

commit.message:
Bind MySQL command parameters as prepared statements

With MariaDB Connector/C, which the installer ships, a command with parameters
now runs as a prepared statement, and its values are bound instead of written
into the SQL. That is the last database client whose values were written into
the SQL, apart from Oracle's libmysql.dll, which hMailServer still loads when
libmariadb.dll is missing and which keeps the escaped literals of
GenerateFromCommand.

- MySQLStatement prepares, binds and executes a command, and reads its result
  set with every column fetched as a string, so the recordset reads it as it
  reads a query's rows. A value longer than its buffer is fetched again in full.
  It is the only file that includes the MariaDB headers, for MYSQL_BIND and
  MYSQL_FIELD; the functions still come through MySQLInterface, which now also
  resolves the mysql_stmt_* functions.
- SQLStatement::ToPositionalParameters can write MySQL's ? placeholders: one per
  occurrence, so a parameter used twice is bound twice. Its test covers them.
- MySQLConnection::GetSupportsCommandParameters is true with the MariaDB client.
  TryExecute and MySQLRecordset::TryOpen run a command that still has parameters
  as a statement; the error number mapping is shared with the query path.
- The regression tests store values made of SQL quotes, backslashes, comment
  markers, parameter names and placeholders, and read them back, and log on as
  an account whose address contains a quote. CI runs them on SQL Server
  Compact, PostgreSQL and MySQL.
- The upgrade-mariadb skill lists the new include directories and exports.

Commands without parameters (SET NAMES, USE, SHOW, the internal scripts) are
still sent as queries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
